name: SLAC-mQ
summary: SLAC-mQ operated at SLAC, Menlo Park, California. This early dedicated small-charge-particle search used an apparatus distinct from SLAC E137.
detection_principle: An electron beam dump produces candidate particles, while downstream low-threshold scintillators seek weak ionization; the same historical data have also been interpreted as dark-matter–electron scattering.

results.summary: The original experiment set limits on millicharged particles.
Historical data constrain light-dark-matter models, rather than representing renewed operation.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered. This record includes reinterpretations of historical data in new models. A reinterpretation paper's publication year is not the apparatus operating year, and the original experiment may primarily have targeted neutrinos, axions or other light particles.
